hero.headline: Indian River County families can apply for free or reduced-price student meals starting July 15
hero.teaser: Families in Indian River County are able to apply for free or reduced price meals for students starting July 15.
hero.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15 by visiting the district's online portal.

Students at six Indian River County schools will automatically receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on their household size and income levels. District officials are encouraging families to complete one application per household to determine their eligibility for the meal programs.

To apply, families must visit www.LINQConnect.com to either sign in to an existing account or create a new one. Once logged in, they need to search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach. Parents must add their student to the application using the Student ID number and the child's formal name as it appears in FOCUS, the district's student information system. From the website homepage, families can access the application by clicking School Services at the top menu and then selecting Free and Reduced Meal Application.

The application process requires families to provide information about household size and income to determine eligibility for the federal nutrition programs. By submitting a single application for all children in the household, families can streamline the process and find out if they qualify for free meals, reduced-price meals, or neither option. The program aims to ensure that students have access to nutritious meals during the school day regardless of their family's financial situation.

Families who have questions about the meal programs or need assistance with the application process can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director. O'Keefe can be reached by phone at (772) 564-5041 or by email at shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org. District officials recommend that families apply as early as possible to ensure their eligibility status is determined before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District terminates 3 firefighters after hazing investigation involving electric shocks
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District on Saturday released investigative reports detailing allegations of hazing and workplace misconduct that led to the termination of 3 firefighters and the suspension of 2 others. District administrators first received videos in March 2026 showing what they described as senior firefighters using a modified bug zapper to administer electric shocks to probationary and apprentice firefighters while on duty. The district said the incidents occurred during shifts in March and September 2024.

The videos prompted Fire Chief Jeff Lee to hire an outside attorney to conduct an independent investigation rather than handle the matter internally. Attorney J.K. Keller, of Allen, Norton & Blue, concluded that a preponderance of the evidence showed probationary employees had been subjected to hazing by senior firefighters and supervisors. Keller also determined the conduct violated multiple district policies, including workplace violence and employee conduct rules. The district said it followed Keller's recommendations by terminating 3 employees and issuing 48-hour unpaid suspensions to 2 others.

The investigative report describes videos showing probationary firefighters being questioned while connected to the modified device and receiving electrical shocks when they answered incorrectly. Other videos allegedly show probationary firefighters voluntarily allowing themselves to be shocked while coworkers looked on. Investigators concluded that any claimed consent was undermined by the power imbalance between senior firefighters and probationary employees.

The media advisory also includes a separate 2025 workplace culture assessment by attorney Susan Gainey, who found Station 1A had an environment marked by intense peer pressure, social exclusion and light hazing that blurred the line between camaraderie and misconduct. Although that earlier investigation did not substantiate harassment claims, Gainey recommended reassigning personnel and implementing additional leadership and workplace culture training. The disciplined employees have exercised their contractual rights to challenge the actions through the grievance and arbitration process. The district said it will confidently present these documented facts within that legal forum and will have no further public comment at this time.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian as severe weather batters Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon in Sebastian on Friday afternoon as severe weather brought heavy rain, lightning strikes and fires across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County.
cards.body:
Videos sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area. Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. She described how all of a sudden it got black, the wind started raging and the sky had lit up like she had not seen.

St. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. At the time of the storm, radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area. St. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. Severe weather stretched all the way to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Moore O'Rourke said it was radical and a little scary.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Cardinals even series against St. Lucie Mets with Saturday win
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Cardinals defeated the St. Lucie Mets on Saturday, forcing a decisive series finale scheduled for Sunday. Palm Beach built an early lead and held off a late rally by St. Lucie to even the series.

The Cardinals jumped ahead early in the game before the Mets mounted a late comeback attempt. Palm Beach managed to protect its advantage despite the St. Lucie surge, securing the victory and tying the series at one game apiece.

The matchup between the two Florida-based Minor League teams has now come down to a winner-take-all game. Both teams will face off Sunday to determine the series champion.

The decisive third game will take place Sunday at the St. Lucie Mets home field. Fans can attend the finale to see which team advances.

cards.headline: Cardinals Homer Twice, Defeat St. Lucie Mets 7-4
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened the three-game series at one game apiece and set up a rubber match Sunday afternoon.

Palm Beach opened the scoring with three runs in the bottom of the first inning. Brayden Smith singled to center field, and an error by D'Andre Smith allowed the Cardinals to capitalize. Ryan Weingartner and Sebastian Dos Santos scored on the play before Brayden Smith came around to give Palm Beach a 3-0 advantage.

St. Lucie responded with two runs in the second inning.

Chase Meggers delivered an RBI single with runners on the corners, scoring AJ Salgado. Jeremy Rodriguez then brought Simon Juan home on a fielder's choice to cut the Cardinals' lead to 3-2.

Palm Beach began pulling away in the fourth inning. Alex Birg drove in Yordalin Pena with an RBI single before Dos Santos launched a two-run home run. The Cardinals eventually built a 7-2 lead.

The Mets bullpen settled the game down after Joe Scarborough entered from the bullpen. Scarborough delivered two scoreless and hitless innings while striking out four batters.

It marked Scarborough's second consecutive scoreless appearance at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Antonio Jimenez gave the Mets another run in the top of the sixth inning with a solo home run. It was Jimenez's sixth homer of the season and his fourth during July, cutting the Palm Beach lead to 7-3.

Caden Wooster followed Scarborough with another strong relief appearance. Wooster allowed just one hit over two scoreless innings and struck out four.

Scarborough and Wooster combined to strike out eight batters over four shutout innings. St. Lucie's pitching staff finished the game with 12 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the second consecutive night.

The Mets mounted one final rally in the ninth inning and brought the potential tying run to the plate. Palm Beach reliever Nathan Shinn escaped the threat and secured the victory for the Cardinals.

St. Lucie fell to 7-14 in the second half and 40-47 overall. Palm Beach improved to 13-9 in the second half and 65-42 overall.

The teams will decide the series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK flights in September due to low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. However, he noted the door is not closed on the route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

Dambeck said the Boston route is seeing great demand and performing well. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

hero.headline: Florida Panthers to open 2026-27 season with four-game road trip
hero.teaser: The Florida Panthers will begin their 2026-27 NHL regular season on the road against the Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29.
hero.body:
The Florida Panthers will begin their 2026-27 NHL regular season with a four-game road trip against Western Conference opponents. The Panthers open against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29, then continue their road swing with a stop in San Jose on Oct. 6.

After completing the road trip, the Panthers will return to South Florida for their home opener on Saturday, Oct. 10, when they welcome the Minnesota Wild to Amerant Bank Arena. December will be particularly busy with seven home games, including four special holiday matchups to close out 2026. The Panthers will host the Buffalo Sabres as part of the holiday schedule. Fans will enjoy two consecutive five-game homestands during the season, with the first running Dec. 19-30 and the second scheduled from March 2-12.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence in game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball has made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night to prevent artificial intelligence from helping make in-game decisions.
cards.body:
The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant general managers and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record at London Diamond League
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr of Great Britain ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999.
cards.body:
Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 at Saturday's Diamond League event in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999. Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record. Earlier in the week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kenyan runner Faith Kipyegon also attempted to become the first woman to run a sub-4-minute mile, though she fell short. Her time of 4:06.42 would have broken the women's world record had it been set during an official competition.

cards.headline: World Cup final tickets in New Jersey start at $7,700 for Argentina-Spain match
cards.teaser: The cheapest ticket on resale sites for Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain in New Jersey costs about $7,700, nearly identical to what the median U.S. household earns in one month.
cards.body:
Lower bowl seats at the stadium require buyers to spend at least $10,000. FIFA has faced criticism over the high ticket prices, which the organization says reflect strong global demand.

Tickets for the third-place game in Miami start at about $700. According to Forbes, this year's World Cup final could end up being the most expensive sports ticket in U.S. history.

President Trump will attend the trophy presentation, with White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt saying his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure and most successful World Cup in American history. The final is a Level 1 Special Event with the highest possible security designation.

cards.headline: World Cup boosts U.S. beer sales 14% in host cities during tournament
cards.teaser: Beer sales in bars, restaurants, stadiums and other venues rose 14% in U.S. host cities during the first four weeks of the World Cup compared to the same period last year, according to the Beer Institute.
cards.body:
In the first four weeks of the tournament, beer sales in bars, restaurants, stadiums and other venues rose 14% in U.S. host cities compared to the same period last year, according to the Beer Institute. The bump extended beyond host cities, with sales up 4% nationally during the tournament. Bars in Boston reported needing emergency deliveries to keep taps from running dry on some game days, while fans downed a total of 290,000 stadium beers during the six matches in Philadelphia, FIFA organizers said.

Jim Koch, the brewer, founder and CEO of the Boston Beer Co., which makes Samuel Adams and other brands, said the company made two emergency deliveries to its Sam Adams Boston Taproom on the first day Scotland's fans were in town. At one point, the taproom was pouring a Sam Adams Boston Lager every 12 seconds. The tournament sales boost comes despite beer consumption falling steadily for a decade in the U.S., according to the Brewers Association, a trade group for craft brewers. Last year was the first time in Gallup's polling that a majority of Americans, 53%, said drinking one or two drinks a day was bad for one's health. Economic worries also have taken a toll, with consumption of all types of alcohol, including wine and spirits, falling 5% last year, beverage market research company IWSR said.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis Jr. join Miami Heat in major trade
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat introduced two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo and forward Bobby Portis Jr. at the Kaseya Center on Thursday, with both players receiving standing ovations from fans.
cards.body:
Thursday afternoon, loud chants of "Giannis" filled the Kaseya Center as the Miami Heat introduced their latest acquisitions. Heat Head Coach Erik Spoelstra said Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Giannis Antetokounmpo, and he said yes. The move brings a two-time MVP, NBA champion, and Finals MVP to South Florida, though questions remain about whether the Heat gave up too much for the star coming off back-to-back injury-filled seasons. Antetokounmpo, who stands 6'11 and weighs 240 pounds, told reporters he thrives on pressure and needs it at this point in his career to go to the next level and get out of his comfort zone. He said he was not there to talk about measurables but rather how many championships he can help bring to Miami. Antetokounmpo said he feels like whenever he puts his mind to something, he usually accomplishes it, and this is the best route for him to win more titles.

The Heat also introduced forward Bobby Portis Jr., who said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better and has been coming off the bench his whole career as a sixth man type of guy. Portis said being aggressive is what he has always been about, a mindset that Riley and Spoelstra believe embodies the Miami Heat way of playing basketball. Portis, who has been playing with Antetokounmpo for six years, said his relationship with Bam Adebayo has been built off being competitors. Spoelstra said the squad featuring Antetokounmpo, Portis, and Adebayo will play a lot of positionless basketball. Antetokounmpo told reporters he wants to be coached hard so everyone else will follow, adding he does not want feedback sugar-coated and needs the truth so he can apply it to his game.
